question: Which Linux companion architecture and ownership model should become officially supported, and should this umbrella be split into separate Windows and Linux delivery trackers?
rationale: The viable GTK/C and cross-platform approaches carry materially different security, dependency, packaging, native-integration, and maintenance obligations that automation cannot choose.

options.title: Sponsor native GTK Linux
options.body: Select the GTK/C direction, assign an owner, and require threat-model, packaging, update, and staged parity proof before official distribution.

options.title: Adopt shared desktop framework
options.body: Choose a Tauri-style shared shell for faster delivery while explicitly accepting and reviewing its dependency and native-integration tradeoffs.

options.title: Keep Linux community-owned
options.body: Track Windows separately and leave Linux implementations external until an official architecture and long-term owner are available.

recommendation.title: Sponsor native GTK Linux
recommendation.body: Select the GTK/C direction, assign an owner, and require threat-model, packaging, update, and staged parity proof before official distribution.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue history shows this person setting the desired Linux product direction and calibrating app priority against core and security work.
